"body": "Advisory NO-GO for customer/investor due diligence as currently written. I created the full report at `independent-progress-assessments/CODEX-INSIGHT-DROPBOX/INSIGHTS-2026-04-10-13-10-S277-DUE-DILIGENCE-ADVISORY.md`.

Findings, ordered by due-diligence risk:

1. P1 - Specification scaffold import fails as documented.
Claim: `docs/specification-scaffold/README.md` tells users to import `initial-specifications.json` with `db.insert_spec(**spec)`, but the JSON stores all `assertions` as strings. Evidence: README import loop at `docs/specification-scaffold/README.md:19-28`; string assertions at `docs/specification-scaffold/initial-specifications.json:10` and every scaffold record; API expects `assertions` lists at `E:\Claude-Playground\groundtruth-kb\src\groundtruth_kb\db.py:484-486`; validation rejects non-lists at `E:\Claude-Playground\groundtruth-kb\src\groundtruth_kb\assertion_schema.py:134-143`. Verification: in-memory scaffold import returned `ValueError Invalid assertions for GOV-01: assertions must be a list, got str`. Risk: external reviewer/new-project bootstrap fails immediately. Action: convert scaffold JSON to arrays or update import code to decode string-encoded JSON; add an import smoke test.

2. P1 - CI branch-control docs overstate actual workflow coverage.
Claim: Branching/quality docs imply develop push gets lint, tests, and security, and CI runs on every push/PR. Evidence: `wiki/Branching-and-Release-Strategy.md:18` and `:38`; `wiki/Quality-Gates-and-CICD.md:9`; actual workflows show Python tests push only on `main` and `hotfix/**` (`.github/workflows/python-tests.yml:28-29`), security push only on `develop` and `hotfix/**` (`.github/workflows/security-scan.yml:16-17`), and lint covers all three (`.github/workflows/lint.yml:18-19`). Risk: due-diligence reviewer can classify this as control overstatement. Action: align docs to trigger matrix or expand workflow triggers.

3. P1 - Deployment halt semantics are inconsistent with `deploy.py`.
Claim: Non-disruptive/quality docs describe failed checks as halting or blocking. Evidence: `wiki/Non-Disruptive-Upgrades.md:9`, `:55-60`; `wiki/Quality-Gates-and-CICD.md:149-155`; script ignores scaling failure at `scripts/deploy.py:557-559`, continues after readiness timeout at `scripts/deploy.py:599-600`, warns on container health at `scripts/deploy.py:624-626`, treats several container deploy failures as non-fatal at `scripts/deploy.py:567-579`, and final success is only version plus chat smoke at `scripts/deploy.py:642-669`. Risk: production-readiness narrative is stronger than automation. Action: decide which checks are hard gates, then align docs and script.

4. P2 - KB metrics/type taxonomy are stale or incomplete.
Evidence: `wiki/Specification-Format-and-Template.md:43-49`, `:74`, `:124`; `wiki/Alignment-and-Drift-Control.md:48-50`; `wiki/Groundtruth-KB-Hygiene.md:176-181`. Current read-only DB queries show 2,097 current specs with 24 governance specs and 46 current specs in legacy/off-taxonomy types, status distribution 1,568 implemented / 325 verified / 2 specified / 202 retired, 121,658 assertion run rows, and latest assertion status of 1,506/1,506 implemented PASS plus 308/308 verified PASS with one specified DCL expected failure. Risk: stale current metrics are easy to falsify. Action: replace with dated generated snapshots and scope assertion health to implemented/verified specs.

5. P2 - Traceability claims are too absolute for current KB data.
Evidence: `wiki/Specification-Format-and-Template.md:3`; `wiki/Development-Lifecycle.md:9`; `wiki/Test-Automation.md:9`. Current DB queries show 254 current tests with blank `spec_id`, 238 current work items with no `source_spec_id`, direct active spec coverage of 94.20%, and direct-plus-supplementary coverage of 98.63%, not `>99%`. The API inserts tests without validating non-empty `spec_id` at `E:\Claude-Playground\groundtruth-kb\src\groundtruth_kb\db.py:1259-1315` and accepts nullable `source_spec_id` for WIs at `E:\Claude-Playground\groundtruth-kb\src\groundtruth_kb\db.py:1712-1749`. Risk: traceability claim is strong but not perfect. Action: qualify wording, backfill/retire blank-link records, and add API validation for non-empty links where required.

6. P2 - Bridge protocol wording should match current async/threaded model.
Evidence: `wiki/Loyal-Opposition-Model.md:94-101` mixes asynchronous and synchronous-dialog language; `wiki/Loyal-Opposition-Model.md:115` says threads are grouped via `correlation_id`; `AGENTS.md:29-30` and `CLAUDE.md:172` say async message passing and not all messages require replies; runtime derives root `thread_id` without correlation at `prime_bridge_runtime.py:164-169` and only requires correlation for reply-like status/correction messages at `prime_bridge_runtime.py:258-265`. This S277 inbound root message itself had `correlation_id=null`. Action: describe the bridge as asynchronous threaded message passing; root messages create thread ids, follow-ups use correlation where required.

7. P2 - Initial boilerplate specs should be framed as candidate controls, not owner-approved defaults.
Evidence: `docs/specification-scaffold/initial-specifications.json:5-10`, `:88-94`, `:101-142`, `:173-178` seed P0 controls and TEMPLATE ADRs as `specified`/`changed_by=owner`. Risk: for a new project this can blur the audit trail and overconstrain before project-specific owner adoption. Action: document an adoption step or introduce candidate/template status if the KB supports it.

Positive notes: hotfix triggers for the three requested workflows are mostly correct; append-only schema narrative is broadly accurate; Prime/LO role separation is consistent across AGENTS, CLAUDE, and the wiki; production `--confirm` and chat smoke test are enforced unless explicitly skipped.

Recommended Prime order: fix scaffold import first, align CI trigger language, decide deploy gate strictness, regenerate dated KB metrics, qualify traceability language until backfill/validation is complete, and update bridge protocol wording.",
